*The rates quoted in this report were obtained by Reuters on a confidential basis from a range of airlines, large forwarders and smalle agents based at the Paris airports.
*All prices are quoted in French francs.
*The tariffs represent average rates calculated from a range of prices and are indicative of current market activity. Ex-Paris air rates stable ahead of March 1 rises By Stuart
Todd

PARIS, Feb 7 (Reuter) - A surge of "spot" activity has had the temporary effect of taking some ex-Paris air cargo rates lower but generally the market has remained stable knowing many rates will be increased on March one, a Reuters survey showed.
The spot discounting was mainly was mainly for heavy-size shipments and was viewed as normal market behaviour after the traditional end-of-year capacity-squeeze

"The beginning of the year is always a bit of a delicate period with demand weak and capacity abundant, the fear being that the "discounting" such conditions engenders will lead to the collapse of rates making the road to recovery a long one," a Far east carrier said.
"However, over the past few weeks these fears have been allayed with a firming of demand which in our case, has given us scope to introduce rates increases in the spring," he added.
One major forwarder told Reuters that it had been notified by Air France of increases on a number of routes notably India, South-East Asia and South America, effective March 1.

"Ex-Paris India rates are set to rise by 20 percent taking the average per kilo rate to between six and seven francs. However, India is very much a case apart, rates having traditionally been fixed at a very low level. Generally speaking, Air France is probably going to implement increases of between five and ten percent."
Air France's rates on routes to the U.S. and South Africa would remain stable, the forwarder said.
Air France's increases are similar to those announced by Lufthansa, KLM and Cargolux.
Other carriers increasing rates from March 1 are Iberia and Aerolineas Argentinas, Latin America being a strong growth sector for ex-Paris air cargo.
In the Middle East sector, Emirates is to increase ex-Paris rates by between five and ten percent from the beginning of next month.

On the long-depressed transatlantic routes, more than one Paris-based belly carrier points to continuing market recovery with the strengthening dollar playing its part. However, apart from a few exceptions there is still hesitation on increasing rates.
"For us, it's not a question of "if", more one of when and by how much," one U.S. airline said.
Air Canada is to increase its ex-Paris cargo rates to Montreal, Toronto and selected destinations in the U.S. by 30 centimes/kilo, effective March 1.

"The increases work out at around five percent and have been made possible by the steady recovery in the market since October 1996 following a prolonged period of downward pressures on rates," a Paris-based Air Canada cargo official told Reuters.

During a temporary lull in ex-Paris traffic volumes to the Asian sector due to the Chinese New Year and Ramadan, two main deck carriers, Thai Airways and Korean Airlines have decided to increase rates by between five and seven percent from March 1 and April 1 respectively.
Malaysian Airline System is to increase its rates by five percent from the beginning of next month, the first time since October 1995.

"This has more to do with what other carriers operating in the sector are doing and a management directive to improve yields rather than a real upturn in the market. However, we are hoping that the spring will bring a sustainable recovery."

Meanwhile, a Singapore Airlines SIA.SI decision on rates is imminent and the carrier has already said it will be introducing an extra Paris-Singapore freighter flight from the end of March in conjunction with Air France.
This in response to strong demand forecasts for 1997.
On Paris-Japan routes, both JAL and ANA applied rates increases last month of between three and four percent.
Along with airlines and forwarders, there is renewed confidence among shippers that favourable economic conditions should prevail in the months ahead.

French luxury travel goods manufacturer, Louis Vuitton Malletier, said it was optimistic its volume of export traffic for the current year, the vast majority transported by air, will exceed 1996 levels.

Vuitton's Transport manager, Bernard Goerens, told Reuters: "We are optimistic on the market outlook for 1997. The strengthening yen and dollar in relation to the French franc can only improve the purchasing power of our major customers. During the course of the year, Vuitton plans to open several new sales outlets, notably in Dubai and Hanoi, which will boost our air cargo volumes. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
